<sup>b</sup> אֲחָזֹו דם he had an attack of congestion. Y. Pes. I, 28
<sup>b</sup> אֲחוּזַת הדם the animal attacked with congestion. Y. Sabb. XIV, 14
<sup>c</sup> bot. אֲחָזַתֹּו עין a pain in the eye seized him. Ib. XIX, end, 17
<sup>b</sup> אחזתו חמה fever overtook him; a. fr.—אָחַז בְּ־ 
<italic>to have a hold of</italic>.—B. Mets. I, 1. Y. Yoma II, 39
<sup>c</sup> top; a. fr.—Part. pass. אָחוּז 
<italic>holding fast, having a firm hold</italic>. Ex. R. s. 46 (v. אֲחַד).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>

<sup>b</sup>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>

<italic>kindling chips</italic>)

<sup>b</sup> sq.) ומַאֲחִיזִין ed. (Mss., Ar. a. Y. ib. beg. 4
<sup>c</sup> ומחזין, ed. Ven. ומחיזין); v. חָזָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="A01023">
<head-word>אחי, </head-word>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (√חו, cmp. חבב) 
<italic>to unite</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Part. pass. אָחוּי 
<italic>united</italic>. Num. R. s. 13, beg. שיהיו אֲחוּיִים אצלו they shall be united with him (around his table).</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִיחָה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to join; to sew together</italic> (with fine stitches); cmp. חוּט; חוּד I.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 39 beg. אברהם שאֹ' את וכ' Abraham who united all mankind into a brotherhood (by the belief in one God), כזה שהוא מְאָחֶה וכ' like one who sews &c., v. infra. Ex. R. s. 40, end.—Esp. 
<italic>to mend, by stitching, the rent of the garment torn in mourning</italic>. M. Kat. 22
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr. Ib. 26
<sup>a</sup> לאַחֹותָן to stitch them together.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa. a. Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְאָחֶה, נִתְאָחֶה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be joined; to be stitched together</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 13, beg. (play on אחותי Cant. V, 1) נִתְאָחוּ לי וכ' they were joined to me (I joined them) in the captivity. Gen. R. s. 68 מִתְאָחֹות, v. אֶבֶן. M. Kat. 26
<sup>a</sup> אין מתאחין must not be stitched together.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be joined by grafting, to grow together</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Kil. I, 27
<sup>a</sup> top הן נתא' וכ' they (the two seeds) combine. Y. Shebi. II, end, 34
<sup>a</sup> bot. Y. Orl. I, 61
<sup>a</sup> bot.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> v. foreg.), pl. constr.</definition>
<notes> אַחֲרֵי 
<italic>after, behind</italic>. Gen. R. s. 44 wherever the Bible uses the preposition 
<italic>a</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>aré</italic> סמוך, it means 
<italic>in connection with</italic>, אחר מופלג while 
<italic>a</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>ar</italic> means without connection (
<italic>later on</italic>). Yoma 6
<sup>a</sup> אחר א' after ‘after’, i.e. some time after the act, opp. חד אחר one ‘after’, immediately, v. אֶוְתִּיוֹס.—לְאַחֲרָיו, לְאַחֲרֶיהָ, מֵאַחֲרָיו, מֵאַחֲרֶיהָ after it, as concluding, opp. לפניה, לפניו introductory (prayer).—Ber. I, 4 אחת לא' one benediction after the Sh’ma. Ib. III, 4 לאחריו (prayer) after meal; a. fr.—כִּלְאַחַר יד as if doing a thing with the back of the hand, i.e. in a manner different from the usual way of doing it. Sabb. 153
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—מֵאַחַר </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (conj. followed by ש־ or ד־) 
<italic>after, since, whereas, because</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 29
<sup>a</sup> מא' ששנינו after it has once been stated in the Mishnah … why was it necessary (?) &c. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> ומאחר דאפי' וכ' and since it is not even rabbinically unfit, why &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> a legal term, 
<italic>mea</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>ar</italic>, the presumption of the truth of one’s statement, 
<italic>because</italic> he might have pleaded more profitably, if he had been inclined to lie.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shebu. VI, 36
<sup>d</sup> bot. אין אומרים בממון מא' מאחר וכ' in money matters we do not apply the principle of 
<italic>mea</italic>
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>er</italic>, so as to say that because he might have said ‘thou hast not lent me anything’, he may say, ‘thou didst lend me, but I paid half of it’ (and his plea must be accepted without an oath); v. מִיגּוֹ s. v. גּוֹ.—אַחֲרֶיךָ 
<italic>thy successor</italic>. Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>c</sup> top יהודה בני א' וכ' my son Judah shall succeed thee, none else (is worthy). Keth. 95
<sup>b</sup> my property I bequeath to thee ואַחֲרַיִיךְ לפ' and after thee it shall go over to …—אַחַר כָּךְ (abbrev. אח"כ) 
<italic>afterwards, subsequently</italic>. Pes. X, 2; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
